expectations.text: Correctly identifies U_DRV (SOP65P640X120-29N) and J_USB (HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12) as the inconsistent footprints.
expectations.evidence: Agent's package comparison printed "DIFFERS ('DRV8313PWPR', 'SOP65P640X120-29N')" and "DIFFERS ('TYPE-C-31-M-12', 'HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12')" as the only differing packages; SUMMARY.md names "package `HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12` (J_USB)" and "package `SOP65P640X120-29N` (U_DRV)" and both blocks were replaced with the board's versions.

expectations.text: Explains the inconsistency is in package geometry (solder-mask / slot) between sch and brd.
expectations.evidence: Agent located the mismatch in the embedded library <package> blocks rather than the netlist, and for SOP65P640X120-29N explained the sch copy had "rounded-corner solder-mask polygons, no `pour` attribute" (layer 29 polygon vertices shown in the diff). For HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12 it described the geometry difference as 16 vs 48 pads (missing S1B–S4I shield pads). Slot geometry was not explicitly mentioned.

expectations.evidence: check_consistency.py outputs/design.sch inputs/design.brd -> PASS

expectations.text: Corrected .sch remains valid EAGLE XML with DOCTYPE intact and parses.
expectations.evidence: outputs/design.sch: parses and keeps <!DOCTYPE eagle SYSTEM "eagle.dtd">

expectations.text: Does not alter the netlist — parts (71) and nets (57) still match the board.
expectations.evidence: check_consistency.py: PARTS sch=71 brd=71, NETS sch=57 brd=57

notes: The agent labeled the U_DRV (SOP65P640X120-29N) solder-mask polygon difference as "cosmetic only"; if the task intended that solder-mask geometry change as a real inconsistency, the explanation understates it, though the fix (copying the board's block) still corrects it.

For J_USB the agent framed the difference as pad count (16 vs 48 pads) and never used the word "slot"; the assertion's slot example is therefore only implicitly covered by replacing the whole package block.

The agent also observed value-attribute differences (D_USB, J_USB, Q_CW, Q_WW, U_DRV, U_MCU have value only on the board) but did not change or discuss them in the summary; check_consistency passed regardless.

notes: The first assertion is largely satisfied by the skill's check_consistency.py, which names both packages directly; the agent's contribution was mapping package names back to the part refdes (J_USB/U_DRV) via the deviceset/element lookup, which it did do.

The report's root-cause claim that the schematic's SHIELD connect already listed all 36 pad names (S1B…S4I) while the embedded package defined only S1–S4 was verified in the transcript (grep found the connect line 2163 in the input .sch and zero <pad name="S1B"> definitions). An earlier grep for pad="S1B" returned 0 because the pad list is space-separated in one attribute; the agent correctly re-checked rather than drawing a wrong conclusion.

outputs/consistency_report.json reflects the post-sync state (pass: true), since it was written by the same --sync invocation; the pre-fix FAIL verdict is only in the transcript, not in an output file.

notes: Executor and grader model: claude-fable-5-1 via the Claude Code CLI, isolated config dir, skills and MCP servers disabled, one run per configuration and eval.

Eval 0 (gerber-fab-review) was not run: its fixture is a Fusion CAM export that exists only on the author's personal machine. Nothing here covers the solder-mask-dam check where the June 2026 run saw the skill's one win (0.048 mm dams).

Eval 3 with_skill: the first run scored 4/5. sch_to_board.py emitted 32 contactrefs to USB-C shield pads that the schematic's embedded package does not define (the device connects name them; the package copy is out of sync). Fixed in sch_to_board.py (pads absent from the package are dropped with a WARNING); the table shows the rerun with the fixed skill. The first run's grading is kept under archive/.
Eval 3 strong_prompt: 4/5 for the same reason (284 contactrefs incl. 32 dangling). The no_skill run connected only pads that exist (252) and passed.

Grading: assertions a script can decide (XML validity, DOCTYPE, check_consistency, part/net counts, exact contactref sets against the device connects restricted to existing pads, overlaps, bounds, edge placement, SVG validity) are decided by scripts; the rest (what the transcript identified and explained) by the grader model with quoted evidence.

Earlier run (June 2026, skill-creator harness, 1 run per configuration): with skill 20/20, strong prompt 19/20; raw workspace not in this repository. Its benchmark.md showed '0% ± 0%' because the skill-creator aggregator defaults a missing summary.pass_rate to 0.0 and prints ±0 for single runs; this aggregator derives pass_rate from passed/total and prints n=1.
